run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Hotel Reservation
Namespace: hotel-reservation

A hotel reservation application built with Go and gRPC, providing backend in-memory and persistent databases, a recommender system for hotel recommendations, and a functionality to place reservations.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: In the sampled data (the observability stack and the hotel-reservation namespace were both created around 2026-11-21T12:47-12:49Z, so the only window with samples is ~12:49:08-12:49:37) the hotel-reservation application services themselves look healthy: all 20 pods are Running/Ready with 0 restarts, all deployments report Available, every frontend trace sampled (GET /hotels, GET /recommendations, POST /reservation, POST /user, 12:49:23-12:49:36) returned HTTP 200 with no error spans, the rate limiter shows 590 received / 590 completed / 0 rejected / 0 expired, and there are no OOM events or CPU throttling. The one component actually observed failing is the cleanup-controller in namespace hotel-reservation: every ~2s it logs 'ConfigMap reservation-cleanup-token is Terminating; attempting controller-owned cleanup' followed by 'cleanup-controller reconciliation failed: Kubernetes API denied cleanup request with HTTP 403 Forbidden', because the ClusterRole bound to its ServiceAccount only allows get/list/watch on configmaps while the controller PATCHes them. The ConfigMap reservation-cleanup-token stays stuck with deletionTimestamp 12:49:23 and finalizer cleanup.reservations.io/pending-cleanup. Separately, mongodb-rate and mongodb-geo pods have fault-injection scripts (drop admin user / revoke readWrite on rate-db and geo-db) mounted at /scripts, but I found no evidence those faults were executed before the end of the window: both MongoDBs created the admin user with readWrite at 12:49:15-12:49:18, the rate and geo services authenticated successfully and generated their test data, and no 'not authorized'/authentication-failure lines appear in the window. I cannot verify what happened after 12:49:37, so a live MongoDB privilege fault or an app-level failure later in the load test remains unresolved.

claims.text: All 20 pods in namespace hotel-reservation are Running with ready=true and restartCount 0, including frontend, search, rate, geo, profile, recommendation, reservation, user, consul and the mongodb-* pods.

All 20 deployments in hotel-reservation report 1 desired / 1 ready / 1 available replica with no unavailable replicas (frontend, search, rate, geo, profile, recommendation, reservation, user, memcached-*, mongodb-*, consul, cleanup-controller).

Frontend traces sampled between 12:49:23 and 12:49:36 show HTTP GET /hotels and GET /recommendations returning http.status_code=200 (3.8-5.2 ms and 1.7-3.0 ms), with 0 error rows across all 105 shown spans; downstream calls to search, geo, rate, profile, recommendation and reservation appear in the same traces.

Frontend 'HTTP POST /reservation' spans at 12:49:24-12:49:31 all carry http.status_code=200 (5.0-10.2 ms), and the corresponding reservation reservations.Reservation/MakeReservation server spans complete in 3.5-8.9 ms with no error status.
Frontend 'HTTP POST /user' spans at 12:49:23-12:49:36 all carry http.status_code=200 (0.6-1.1 ms) and the user service user.User/CheckUser spans complete in 18-38 microseconds with no error status.

The rate service limiter metrics at 12:49:37 are rate_backend_qps_limit=500, rate_queue_capacity=256, rate_in_flight=0, rate_queue_depth=0, rate_requests_received_total=590, rate_requests_completed_total=590, rate_requests_rejected_total=0 and rate_requests_expired_total=0.

The only error stream found in namespace hotel-reservation over 11:49:37-12:49:37 besides transient frontend start-up Consul connection-refused lines (12:49:08) and routine MongoDB start-up messages is the cleanup-controller's repeated 'Kubernetes API denied cleanup request with HTTP 403 Forbidden' (7 occurrences in the last 2 minutes of the window).

The cleanup-controller pod logs, every ~2 seconds from 12:49:28 to 12:49:36, the pair 'ConfigMap reservation-cleanup-token is Terminating; attempting controller-owned cleanup' and 'cleanup-controller reconciliation failed: Kubernetes API denied cleanup request with HTTP 403 Forbidden'.

The cleanup-controller read 271 log lines up to 12:53:54 and reported 256 of them lying after the 12:49:37 window end, i.e. the same 403 reconciliation loop was still running at the time of the query, not only at start-up.

ConfigMap reservation-cleanup-token in namespace hotel-reservation has deletionTimestamp 2026-11-21T12:49:23Z and finalizer 'cleanup.reservations.io/pending-cleanup', with label app.kubernetes.io/component=reservation-cleanup; it is still present (stuck Terminating) at query time.
ClusterRole 'configmap-cleanup-controller' grants only verbs get, list and watch on core configmaps - it grants no patch or update verb, which is what the controller's reconciliation PATCH requires.

ClusterRoleBinding 'configmap-cleanup-controller' binds ClusterRole configmap-cleanup-controller to ServiceAccount 'cleanup-controller' in namespace hotel-reservation, and the cleanup-controller Deployment runs with serviceAccountName 'cleanup-controller'.

The control script of the cleanup-controller (ConfigMap cleanup-controller-script) issues a PATCH to /api/v1/namespaces/hotel-reservation/configmaps/<name> with a merge patch removing the finalizer list entry, which is precisely the request the API server rejects with 403 Forbidden.

Pods mongodb-rate-56cc8659c9-kqfxv and mongodb-geo-5ff578bcb8-x8k4l mount ConfigMaps failure-admin-rate and failure-admin-geo at /scripts; those ConfigMaps contain scripts that drop the mongo 'admin' user and revoke its readWrite role on rate-db and geo-db (plus mitigation scripts that recreate/grant it).

mongodb-rate logs at 12:49:15 show 'Creating admin user...' and 'Granting readWrite role to admin on rate-db database...', and later successful SCRAM authentications from the rate service (10.244.125.31) at 12:49:17, 12:49:22 and 12:49:33; mongodb-geo logs show the same admin creation/readWrite grant for geo-db at 12:49:16 and successful authentications from the geo service (10.244.7.253) at 12:49:18.

The rate and geo services started cleanly and reached 'Successfully registered in consul' (rate at 12:49:17, geo at 12:49:18) after connecting to their MongoDB and memcached endpoints; the rate service also logged 'Generating test data... Successfull' and the geo service 'New session successfull... / Generating test data... Successfull'.

No container in namespace hotel-reservation has an OOM event (container_oom_events_total = 0 for every pod/container) and no application pod shows CPU throttling (throttled-periods ratio 0 for frontend, search, rate, geo, profile, recommendation, reservation, user).

Every hotel-reservation Service with a endpoints object has ready addresses, e.g. search -> 10.244.7.235:8082/9092, rate -> 10.244.125.31:8084/9091, frontend -> 10.244.7.210:5000, reservation -> 10.244.125.36:8087, user -> 10.244.234.163:8086.

The cleanup-controller failure is caused by its ClusterRole configmap-cleanup-controller being scoped too narrowly (get/list/watch only) for the finalizer-removal PATCH it performs; the controller therefore cannot reconcile the stuck ConfigMap reservation-cleanup-token, and the 403 loop continues indefinitely. This is the deepest cause the evidence supports for the only confirmed malfunction, but it has no demonstrated effect on hotel-reservation request handling.

A MongoDB authorization fault (admin user dropped or readWrite revoked on rate-db and/or geo-db) was staged for this environment via the failure-admin-rate / failure-admin-geo ConfigMaps mounted at /scripts in the mongodb-rate and mongodb-geo pods, and may still be intended to be executed or may have been executed after the last readable sample (12:49:37). No such fault is visible inside the sampled window.

A broad outage or gRPC error burst in the hotel-reservation services is contradicted by the sampled traces: 105 frontend spans between 12:49:23 and 12:49:36 with 0 error rows and only http.status_code=200, and by POST /reservation and POST /user traces all returning 200.

'Frontend cannot reach Consul / services are not registered' is rejected as the incident: the connection-refused lines against consul:8500 occur only at frontend start-up (12:49:08) before Consul was listening, after which the frontend registered its gRPC clients and served 200s, and all service endpoints have ready addresses.

Grant the cleanup-controller's ServiceAccount the missing configmap write verbs (e.g. add patch, and update if the client uses it, for resources=configmaps in ClusterRole configmap-cleanup-controller), then verify the controller removes finalizer cleanup.reservations.io/pending-cleanup from ConfigMap reservation-cleanup-token; alternatively remove that finalizer once it is confirmed the owner is defunct.

Re-check the mongo 'admin' user's roles for rate-db and geo-db (and the presence of the admin user) after the load test, since /scripts/revoke-admin-*-mongo.sh and /scripts/remove-admin-mongo.sh are mounted in both MongoDB pods and would cause 'not authorized' failures in the rate or geo service if executed.

gaps: Prometheus has only a single sample for the application series at 12:49:37 (first scrape after the pods started), so no rate/increase, baseline or trend can be computed for the hotel-reservation app; metrics like traces_span_metrics_calls_total, search_* and up{search} had no usable samples inside 11:49:37-12:49:37 (increase() over one sample returns nothing).

The application pods and the observability stack were created at ~12:47-12:49Z, so there is no history before 12:49:08 and no comparable baseline for latency or error rate; the 24h authorized window contains almost no application data.

Logs and Loki are restricted to the authorized window ending 12:49:37; the cleanup-controller tool reported 256 of its lines and the MongoDB pods a few lines lying after that end, so events after 12:49:37 (including any execution of the staged MongoDB failure scripts and any resulting 'not authorized' errors) could not be read.

Whether a MongoDB admin-privilege fault was actually applied cannot be confirmed: no 'not authorized'/authentication-failure line was returned for hotel-reservation in the window (that query returned no lines, which is a query result, not proof of absence), and secret values/DB user state cannot be read with the available tools.
Whether any workload depends on ConfigMap reservation-cleanup-token is unknown; the deployment specs read did not reference it, but not every volume/mount of every workload was enumerated.
No user-facing impact of the cleanup-controller failure was observed; its blast radius beyond the stuck ConfigMap is unverified.
The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so what changed in the ClusterRole/ConfigMap before the incident cannot be established.
next_steps: Add patch/update verbs on configmaps to ClusterRole configmap-cleanup-controller (or bind the controller to a role that has them) and confirm ConfigMap reservation-cleanup-token disappears.

After the next load-test run, query the search service metrics (search_rate_attempts_total / failures_total / timeouts_total / successes_total) and traces_span_metrics_calls_total{status_code!="OK"} over a window with more than one scrape to look for retry/error bursts against the rate service.
Check the MongoDB admin user's roles for rate-db and geo-db (db.getUser('admin')) to confirm the staged failure-admin-rate / failure-admin-geo scripts were not left applied.

import json
import os
import ssl
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

NAMESPACE = "hotel-reservation"
FINALIZER = "cleanup.reservations.io/pending-cleanup"
LABEL_SELECTOR = "app.kubernetes.io/component=reservation-cleanup"
TOKEN_FILE = [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
CA_FILE = "/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/ca.crt"
API_SERVER = (
    f"https://{os.environ['KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST']}:"
    f"{os.environ['KUBERNETES_SERVICE_PORT_HTTPS']}"
)
TLS_CONTEXT = ssl.create_default_context(cafile=CA_FILE)


def api_request(method, path, payload=None):
    data = None if payload is None else json.dumps(payload).encode()
    headers = [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
    if payload is not None:
        headers["Content-Type"] = "application/merge-patch+json"
    request = urllib.request.Request(
        f"{API_SERVER}{path}",
        data=data,
        headers=[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL],
        method=method,
    )
    with urllib.request.urlopen(request, context=TLS_CONTEXT, timeout=10) as response:
        raw = response.read()
        return json.loads(raw) if raw else {}


def reconcile():
    selector = urllib.parse.quote(LABEL_SELECTOR, safe="")
    response = api_request(
        "GET",
        f"/api/v1/namespaces/{NAMESPACE}/configmaps?labelSelector={selector}",
    )
    for configmap in response.get("items", []):
        metadata = configmap.get("metadata", {})
        finalizers = metadata.get("finalizers", [])
        if not metadata.get("deletionTimestamp") or FINALIZER not in finalizers:
            continue

        name = metadata["name"]
        remaining = [item for item in finalizers if item != FINALIZER]
        print(
            f"ConfigMap {name} is Terminating; attempting controller-owned cleanup",
            flush=True,
        )
        encoded_name = urllib.parse.quote(name, safe="")
        api_request(
            "PATCH",
            f"/api/v1/namespaces/{NAMESPACE}/configmaps/{encoded_name}",
            {"metadata": {"finalizers": remaining}},
        )
        print(f"ConfigMap {name} cleanup completed", flush=True)


print(f"cleanup-controller starting namespace={NAMESPACE}", flush=True)
while True:
    try:
        reconcile()
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as error:
        if error.code == 403:
            print(
                "cleanup-controller reconciliation failed: "
                "Kubernetes API denied cleanup request with HTTP 403 Forbidden",
                flush=True,
            )
        else:
            print(
                f"cleanup-controller reconciliation failed: Kubernetes API returned HTTP {error.code}",
                flush=True,
            )
    except Exception as error:
        print(
            f"cleanup-controller reconciliation failed: {type(error).__name__}",
            flush=True,
        )
    time.sleep(2)

ROOT_USER="root"

ADMIN_USER="admin"

     --eval "db.createUser({user: '$ADMIN_USER', pwd: '$ADMIN_PWD', roles:[{role:'userAdminAnyDatabase',db:'admin'}]});"

echo "Granting readWrite role to $ADMIN_USER on $TARGET_DB database..."
mongo admin -u $ROOT_USER -p $ROOT_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.grantRolesToUser('$ADMIN_USER', [{role: '$READ_WRITE_ROLE', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"

echo "Privileges restored successfully"

#!/bin/bash


ADMIN_USER="admin"
ADMIN_PWD="admin"

ROOT_USER="root"
ROOT_PWD="root"

TARGET_DB="geo-db"
READ_WRITE_ROLE="readWrite"

echo "Waiting for MongoDB to start..."
until mongo --eval "print('waited for connection')" > /dev/null 2>&1; do
  sleep 1
done
echo "MongoDB started"

# Create the admin user (will fail if the user already exists)
echo "Creating admin user..."
mongo admin --eval "db.createUser({user: '$ADMIN_USER', pwd: '$ADMIN_PWD', roles:[{role:'userAdminAnyDatabase',db:'admin'}]});"

# Grant readWrite role on the target database
echo "Granting readWrite role to $ADMIN_USER on $TARGET_DB database..."
mongo admin -u $ADMIN_USER -p $ADMIN_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.grantRolesToUser('$ADMIN_USER', [{role: '$READ_WRITE_ROLE', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"

# Create the root user (will fail if the user already exists)
echo "Creating root user..."
mongo admin --eval "db.createUser({user: '$ROOT_USER', pwd: '$ROOT_PWD', roles:[{role:'userAdminAnyDatabase',db:'admin'}]});"

# Grant readWrite role on the target database to root
echo "Granting readWrite role to $ROOT_USER on $TARGET_DB database..."
mongo admin -u $ROOT_USER -p $ROOT_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.grantRolesToUser('$ROOT_USER', [{role: '$READ_WRITE_ROLE', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"


echo "Initialization script completed"
